next:wr:437.hint: 姉も私もクラシック音楽が好きだ(両方)
next:wr:437.answer: Both my sister and I like classical music.
next:wr:437.fullSentence: Both my sister and I like classical music.
next:wr:437.explanation: both A and B『AとBの両方』。

next:wr:439.hint: 彼女は賢いだけでなく親切でもある
next:wr:439.answer: She is not only smart but also kind.
next:wr:439.fullSentence: She is not only smart but also kind.
next:wr:439.explanation: not only A but (also) B『AだけでなくBも』。
next:wr:439.relatedInfo: alsoは省略されることもある。

next:wr:441.hint: 彼も妻も魚介類が好きではない
next:wr:441.answer: Neither he nor his wife likes seafood.
next:wr:441.fullSentence: Neither he nor his wife likes seafood.
next:wr:441.explanation: neither A nor B『AもBも〜ない』。
next:wr:441.relatedInfo: 動詞は近い方のBに一致させる。

next:wr:444.hint: たとえこの世にあなたしか男性がいなくなっても、あなたとは結婚しない
next:wr:444.answer: I would not marry you if you were the last person on earth.
next:wr:444.fullSentence: I would not marry you if you were the last person on earth.
next:wr:444.explanation: 極端な仮定を表すif節の慣用表現。強い拒絶のニュアンスを表す。
next:wr:444.relatedInfo: 仮定法過去とともに使われる。

next:wr:447.hint: 好きであろうがなかろうが、それをしなければならない
next:wr:447.answer: Whether you like it or not, you have to do it.
next:wr:447.fullSentence: Whether you like it or not, you have to do it.
next:wr:447.explanation: Whether you like it or not, ~『好きであろうがなかろうが〜』。
next:wr:447.relatedInfo: 譲歩を表す副詞節としてのwhether。

next:wr:449.hint: お茶が好きな人もいる一方で、コーヒーを好む人もいる(対比)
next:wr:449.answer: Some people like tea, whereas others prefer coffee.
next:wr:449.fullSentence: Some people like tea, whereas others prefer coffee.
next:wr:449.explanation: whereas『〜である一方で/それに対して』。対比を表す接続詞。
next:wr:449.relatedInfo: whileと同じ対比の意味で使われる。

next:wr:451.hint: 彼はとても疲れていたのですぐに眠ってしまった
next:wr:451.answer: He was so tired that he fell asleep immediately.
next:wr:451.fullSentence: He was so tired that he fell asleep immediately.
next:wr:451.explanation: so ~ that ...『とても〜なので…/…するほど〜』。
next:wr:451.relatedInfo: soの後は形容詞・副詞が続く。

next:wr:453.hint: 彼女の恐怖は大変なものだったので、動けなかった
next:wr:453.answer: Her fear was such that she could not move.
next:wr:453.fullSentence: Her fear was such that she could not move.
next:wr:453.explanation: S is such that ~『Sは大変なものなので〜だ』。
next:wr:453.relatedInfo: such is S that ~ (倒置形)も同じ意味。

next:wr:455.hint: みんなに聞こえるように、もっと大きな声で話して
next:wr:455.answer: Speak louder so that everyone can hear you.
next:wr:455.fullSentence: Speak louder so that everyone can hear you.
next:wr:455.explanation: so that S can/will/may ~『〜するために』(目的)。
next:wr:455.relatedInfo: soとthatを離して so ... that の結果構文と混同しないこと。

next:wr:457.hint: 雨が降るといけないので、傘を持って行きなさい
next:wr:457.answer: Take an umbrella in case it rains.
next:wr:457.fullSentence: Take an umbrella in case it rains.
next:wr:457.explanation: in case S+V『〜するといけないので/〜する場合に備えて』。
next:wr:457.relatedInfo: アメリカ英語ではin case = ifの意味で使われることもある。

next:wr:459.hint: 彼はまた失敗しないように一生懸命働いた
next:wr:459.answer: He worked hard for fear that he should fail again.
next:wr:459.fullSentence: He worked hard for fear that he should fail again.
next:wr:459.explanation: for fear (that) S should do『〜しないように』。that節の中にshouldを使う。
next:wr:459.relatedInfo: shouldは省略されることもある。

next:wr:461.hint: いったん始めると、やめられない
next:wr:461.answer: Once you start, you can't stop.
next:wr:461.fullSentence: Once you start, you can't stop.
next:wr:461.relatedInfo: 時を表す接続詞的な用法。

next:wr:463.hint: 私の知る限り、彼は海外に行ったことがない(範囲)
next:wr:463.answer: As far as I know, he has never been abroad.
next:wr:463.fullSentence: As far as I know, he has never been abroad.
next:wr:463.explanation: as far as『〜する限り(範囲・程度)』。
next:wr:463.relatedInfo: as long as(条件・期間)との使い分けに注意。

next:wr:465.hint: 私のオフィスは10階にある
next:wr:465.answer: My office is on the tenth floor.
next:wr:465.fullSentence: My office is on the tenth floor.
next:wr:465.relatedInfo: 階数にはonを使う(inではない)。

next:wr:467.relatedInfo: onの後は祝う対象の名詞。

next:wr:469.hint: それについて一晩よく考えて、明日答えます
next:wr:469.answer: Let me sleep on it and give you my answer tomorrow.
next:wr:469.fullSentence: Let me sleep on it and give you my answer tomorrow.
next:wr:469.explanation: sleep on ~『〜について一晩よく考える』。
next:wr:469.relatedInfo: 即決を避けるときによく使う表現。

next:wr:471.hint: 状況は10年にわたって変化してきた
next:wr:471.answer: The situation has changed over 10 years.
next:wr:471.fullSentence: The situation has changed over 10 years.

next:wr:473.hint: その犬は車に轢かれそうになった
next:wr:473.answer: The dog was almost run over by a car.
next:wr:473.fullSentence: The dog was almost run over by a car.
next:wr:473.relatedInfo: 受動態run overed…ではなくwas run overの形。

next:wr:475.hint: 会議は今、終わっている
next:wr:475.relatedInfo: overは形容詞的に『終わった状態』を表す。

next:wr:477.hint: 今夜夕食にこちらへ来ませんか
next:wr:477.answer: Why don't you come over for dinner tonight?
next:wr:477.fullSentence: Why don't you come over for dinner tonight?
next:wr:477.explanation: come over『(こちらへ)やって来る』。
next:wr:477.relatedInfo: 訪問を誘う際によく使う句動詞。

next:wr:479.hint: この花瓶は注意深く扱ってください
next:wr:479.answer: Please handle this vase with care.
next:wr:479.fullSentence: Please handle this vase with care.
next:wr:479.relatedInfo: carefullyとほぼ同義の前置詞句。

next:wr:481.hint: 経験を積むにつれて彼の技術は上達した
next:wr:481.explanation: with experience『経験を積むにつれて』。
next:wr:481.relatedInfo: withが比例・付随の変化を表す用法。

next:wr:483.hint: 彼女はその箱の端をつかんで持ち上げた
next:wr:483.answer: She picked up the box by one corner.
next:wr:483.fullSentence: She picked up the box by one corner.
next:wr:483.explanation: pick up ~ by one corner『〜の端をつかんで持ち上げる』。
next:wr:483.relatedInfo: byは接触点・つかむ部分を表す。

next:wr:485.hint: その2つの建物は並んで立っている
next:wr:485.answer: The two buildings stand side by side.
next:wr:485.fullSentence: The two buildings stand side by side.
next:wr:485.explanation: stand side by side『並んで立つ』。
next:wr:485.relatedInfo: side by sideは『並んで』を表す慣用句。

next:wr:487.hint: 彼はいつも何事も規則通りに行う
next:wr:487.answer: He always does everything by the book.
next:wr:487.fullSentence: He always does everything by the book.
next:wr:487.relatedInfo: 融通が利かないことを揶揄するニュアンスもある。
